correctness.rationale: For singleton valuations the complement of the noncontingency output is a two-point information cell, and a second application deletes precisely edges crossing that cell. Equality of such boundary sets forces each two-colored neighborhood into a dyad or an alternating square; converse is proved componentwise, using four-entry XOR parity on squares. Infinite worlds are handled because each local component closes in at most four vertices, not by a finite enumeration. A separate exhaustive Python check verifies all pairs and valuations for labeled sizes one through seven, plus exact coefficient counts.

value.rationale: Two-agent knowing-whether is a natural nonlinear epistemic operator. The result completely identifies when its order of application does not matter under a sharp binary information-cell assumption, for finite and infinite frames, gives a minimal three-world obstruction, and transfers a full labeled census to a logically defined frame class. This is not merely a numerical calculation or a corollary of normal-modal operator commutation.
